probe: does a flat's LEVEL reach the product? — the uniform-card arm, and what it exposed
setup: arm U = the same 125 lights calibrated with skyflat_set-05 divided by a uniform card of 1.05 (Siril fdiv). Verified on the masters: mean(flat_05)/mean(flat_U) = 1.050001, so the card really is in the flat.
mechanism: Siril `calibrate` NORMALIZES the flat by its own level before dividing, so a uniform scale on a flat cannot reach the product. The 5% is gone; what survives is float rounding at the 1e-7 relative level, spread over 74% of the pixels.
why_this_makes_the_floor_NON_VACUOUS: the identity control's floor is exactly zero because the two arms are bit-identical, which a sceptic can call a tautology. This arm is NOT bit-identical — three quarters of its pixels differ, through a genuinely different arithmetic path — and every delivered dipole still reads EXACTLY 0.0000 on both instruments. A change that touches 74% of the pixels moves no dipole.
what_it_adds_to_the_main_result: a flat's absolute LEVEL is removed by the tool itself, so what reaches the object is precisely the flats' relative SHAPE difference — which is what the measurement quantifies.
